method: Official unauthenticated X publishing oEmbed endpoint; establishes returned public post text, not feed delivery or readership.

posts.label: original
posts.author: Goga Koreli
posts.returnedPostText: I gave Linux 4 GB of my Mac's 24 GB RAM: T3 Code dependencies installed in 2.10s vs 8.12s on macOS. Tested four repos, traced the extra file work, and checked fixes for speed, type errors and cache writes. https://t.co/fnj3tFK10h

posts.label: theo-reply
posts.author: Goga Koreli
posts.returnedPostText: I tested this on the same M5 Mac: 2.10s in a 4 GB Linux VM vs 8.12s on macOS for T3 dependencies, with warm caches. Tested four repos and found fixes, type errors, and a build that changed cached package files: https://t.co/fnj3tFK10h

posts.label: install-answer
posts.author: Goga Koreli
posts.returnedPostText: Yes, the chart times pnpm install in a new worktree. Bare git worktree creation is separate; I measured only the install step, with warm caches, across T3, Next.js, Vite and SvelteKit: https://t.co/fnj3tFK10h

posts.label: filesystem-answer
posts.author: Goga Koreli
posts.returnedPostText: ZFS wasn't required in my tests: an ext4 Linux VM on the same Mac beat macOS in all four repos. Moving the cache onto the checkout's filesystem cut a separate XFS test from 7.6s to 1.4s; this doesn't isolate APFS alone. https://t.co/fnj3tFK10h
